mechanisms.name: Experiential Avoidance
mechanisms.definition: Attempts to alter, escape, or suppress unwanted internal experiences even when doing so increases long-term suffering.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Often develops through learning that distress can be reduced quickly by escape, distraction, or control.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Short-term relief reinforces avoidance while valued action, exposure, and emotional processing are narrowed over time.
client_signals: I change the subject when feelings rise.
I stay busy so I do not have to feel.
I leave situations when emotion starts.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Avoidance may spike when distress is approached too quickly without safety.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration often requires practicing willingness after session openness.

mechanisms.name: Cognitive Fusion
mechanisms.definition: Excessive entanglement with thoughts such that thoughts are treated as literal commands or facts.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Language and threat-learning can teach the mind to treat thoughts as reality rather than mental events.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Fused thoughts drive rigid behavior, rumination, and avoidance of disconfirming experience.
client_signals: My mind says I cannot handle this and I believe it.
I get stuck in my thoughts.
I argue with myself for hours.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: High fusion can amplify panic during destabilizing experiences.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Post-session work may focus on observing thoughts without obedience.

mechanisms.name: Shame Sensitivity
mechanisms.definition: Heightened threat response to perceived exposure, defectiveness, or social rejection.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Often shaped by early invalidation, criticism, trauma, or repeated social threat.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Concealment and withdrawal reduce immediate shame but reinforce isolation and self-alienation.
client_signals: I hide parts of myself.
I feel defective when seen.
I withdraw after feeling exposed.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Shame can intensify if the person feels judged or exposed without consent.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration may require shame-aware support and paced disclosure.

mechanisms.name: Harsh Self-Criticism
mechanisms.definition: Persistent hostile or punitive self-evaluation that functions as threat and behavioral control.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: May develop through critical caregiving, bullying, perfectionistic environments, or trauma.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Self-attack is maintained when it is experienced as necessary for improvement or safety.
client_signals: I speak to myself in a way I would never speak to a friend.
Nothing I do is good enough.
I punish myself when I fail.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Self-criticism may spike after difficult session content.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration support often includes compassionate self-talk practice.

mechanisms.name: Rumination
mechanisms.definition: Repetitive, passive analysis of distress, causes, and consequences without effective problem solving.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Can develop when reflection is modeled as the primary coping strategy for uncertainty or threat.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Rumination feels productive but maintains low mood, helplessness, and cognitive fusion.
client_signals: I replay conversations over and over.
I analyze why I feel this way but get nowhere.
I cannot switch my mind off.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Post-session rumination can amplify distress if integration is unstructured.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration plans may include action-first experiments instead of analysis loops.

mechanisms.name: Addictive Relief Cycle
mechanisms.definition: A learned loop where substance or behavior use provides rapid relief from distress and is reinforced over time.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Negative reinforcement and cue learning link distress, craving, use, and temporary relief.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Relief is immediate while withdrawal, shame, and functional costs accumulate later.
client_signals: I use when I cannot tolerate how I feel.
I promise to stop and then relapse under stress.
Craving hits when I am alone or ashamed.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Requires careful screening for active dependence and medical risk.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration must address triggers, support systems, and relapse planning.

mechanisms.name: Pain Catastrophizing
mechanisms.definition: Threat-oriented interpretation of pain involving magnification, helplessness, and rumination about pain.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Often develops through repeated pain episodes, fear learning, and invalidation of bodily experience.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Catastrophic appraisals increase vigilance, avoidance, and disability even when tissue injury is stable.
client_signals: I worry the pain will never stop.
I think the worst when pain increases.
I avoid movement because I fear damage.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Medical assessment and pacing are required before behavioral activation.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration may include gentle re-engagement with movement and meaning.

mechanisms.name: Emotional Suppression
mechanisms.definition: Active inhibition of emotional expression or experience while outward behavior may appear controlled.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Often learned when emotional expression was punished, shamed, or unsafe.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Suppression reduces visible distress short-term but increases physiological load and relational disconnection.
client_signals: I shut down when feelings come up.
People say I seem fine but I feel numb inside.
I push feelings away until I explode.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Suppressed affect may surface abruptly during deep session work.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration often requires titrated emotional contact and co-regulation.

mechanisms.name: Control Strategies
mechanisms.definition: Persistent attempts to regulate internal experience through certainty, checking, reassurance, or rigid rules.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: Develops when unpredictability or threat has been reduced through control in the past.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Control reduces immediate uncertainty but narrows flexibility and increases dependence on safety behaviors.
client_signals: I need to know what will happen.
I repeat rituals until it feels safe.
I seek reassurance when anxiety rises.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Control strategies may intensify when session structure feels unpredictable.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration may practice flexible response to uncertainty.

mechanisms.name: Loss of Meaning
mechanisms.definition: Reduced sense of purpose, coherence, or value-laden direction in life.
mechanisms.how_it_forms: May follow loss, trauma, burnout, chronic stress, or prolonged disconnection from values.
mechanisms.maintaining_logic: Without meaning anchors, avoidance and rumination fill the space and further reduce engagement.
client_signals: Nothing feels worthwhile.
I am just going through the motions.
I do not know who I am anymore.
mechanisms.session_risk_notes: Existential distress requires careful pacing and safety planning.
mechanisms.integration_relevance: Integration often focuses on small values-aligned actions.
